rooms.prompt:
Step through plus1 and make its call to triple.
Press Play, or step one line at a time. Watch ra: it's every function's way back.
rooms.hint: A call has to leave a way back. Which of the two does?
rooms.explanation: jal ra, triple does two things: it puts the address of the line after it in ra, then jumps. triple's jr ra uses that address to come back. j only jumps, so nothing tells triple where to return.

code.note: plus1 makes room for one word on the stack...
...and keeps the Chomper's address there, since ra is about to change. The next room is all about why.

code.ask: plus1 needs triple(x). Make the call:

options.label: jal ra, triple
options.why: jal put the address of the next line in ra, then jumped: triple knows where to come back.

options.label: j triple
options.why: j jumped without leaving a way back, so ra still held the Chomper's address. triple's jr ra went straight back to the Chomper: plus1 never added its 1 or gave back its stack.

code.note: Back in plus1, with triple's answer in a0. Add 1.
Get the Chomper's address back into ra...
...give the stack word back...
...and return to the Chomper.
triple doubles x into t0...
...then adds x once more: 3x, in a0, where return values go.

payload.intro: The Chomper calls plus1(4): a0 = 4, and ra = 0x400, the Chomper's own address, so plus1 can come back.

rooms.prompt:
Step through plus2 and keep its way back safe.
plus2 calls inc twice, and every jal changes ra.
rooms.hint: Each jal ra writes over ra. Where can the Chomper's address wait until plus2 is done?
rooms.explanation: A function that makes calls loses ra at its first jal, so it saves ra in its stack frame first and loads it back just before returning. That pair (the prologue and the epilogue) is the start of every stack frame.

code.ask: plus2 is about to call inc twice, and each jal writes over ra, its only way back to the Chomper. Before the calls, push:

options.label: ra onto the stack
options.why: The Chomper's address is safe at sp+0. The matching lw ra goes just before plus2 returns.

options.label: nothing
options.why: The first jal overwrote ra with an address inside plus2, and nothing had kept the Chomper's. So plus2's jr ra jumped back into plus2 itself, again and again: it never returned.

code.note: First call: ra now points back into plus2.
Second call: ra points into plus2 again. The Chomper's address is only on the stack now.

payload.intro: The Chomper calls plus2(5) with ra = 0x400. Keep an eye on ra as plus2 makes its calls.

rooms.prompt:
Step through plusx and keep x safe across a call.
plusx needs x again after calling inc.
rooms.code_snippet: int plusx(int x) { return inc(x) + x; }
rooms.hint: Any function may change t registers. What can't inc touch?
rooms.explanation: t registers are temporaries: a function called in between may change them, as inc does here. A value needed after a call goes in the caller's own stack frame (or in an s register, next room).

code.note: plusx makes room for two words...
...keeps ra in the top one, and leaves sp+0 free.

code.ask: plusx needs x after calling inc, but a call may change any t or a register. Keep x:

options.label: in t0
options.why: inc used t0 too: when it returned, t0 held inc's own work (6), not x, so plusx returned 12 instead of 11. t registers don't survive a call.

options.label: on the stack, at sp+0
options.why: sp+0 is plusx's own word: inc can't touch it, so x is still there after the call.

code.note: inc works in t0: any function may.

payload.intro: The Chomper calls plusx(5). plusx will need x (5) again after its call.

rooms.prompt:
Step through plusx and keep the Chomper's s0 safe.
This plusx keeps x in s0, a register calls leave alone.
rooms.code_snippet: int plusx(int x) { return inc(x) + x; }
rooms.hint: s0 survives calls because every function that uses it puts it back. Is plusx one of them?
rooms.explanation: s registers are saved registers: a function may use them only if it saves the old value first and puts it back before returning. In exchange, every call it makes leaves them alone, which is why x is still in s0 after jal ra, inc.

code.ask: plusx will keep x in s0 across its call to inc. But s0 belongs to whoever called plusx, and plusx makes a call too. Its frame saves:

options.label: ra and s0
options.why: The Chomper's s0 waits at sp+0 and ra at sp+4; the matching loads go just before plusx returns.

options.label: only ra
options.why: plusx wrote x into s0 without saving the Chomper's s0 first, so the Chomper got its s0 back changed (s0 = 5). A function must save every s register it uses.

options.label: only s0
options.why: With ra not saved, jal ra, inc took plusx's only way back: its return jumped back into plusx, which then read past the top of the stack instead of reaching the Chomper.

code.note: x goes in s0, which inc promises to leave alone.
s0 still holds x after the call.

payload.intro: The Chomper calls plusx(5). Watch s0: it holds the Chomper's own value (0x5A08) to start.

rooms.prompt:
Ride sqr(3) down the tower and back up.
sqr calls itself: every call adds a floor, and every return takes one away.
rooms.code_snippet: int sqr(int x) { return x < 2 ? x : sqr(x - 1) + x + x - 1; }
rooms.hint: Every floor runs the same code. What does each one need to keep for after its call?
rooms.explanation: Recursion works because every call gets its own frame: sqr(3), sqr(2), and sqr(1) each keep their own ra and their own x (in s0) on their own floor. On the way back up, each floor adds x + x - 1 to what the floor below returned: 1, then 4, then 9.

code.ask: sqr calls itself, and keeps x in s0 for after the call. Each floor's frame saves:

options.label: ra and s0
options.why: Every floor will keep its own way back and its caller's s0.

options.label: only ra
options.why: Each inner sqr wrote its own x into s0 and nothing saved the outer one's, so on the way back up every floor added the wrong x, and the Chomper's s0 came back changed.

code.note: Is x less than 2?
If so, x is the answer: skip to the end.
Keep x in s0 for after the call.
The argument for the next floor: x - 1.
sqr calls itself: one floor down.
Back up a floor: sqr(x - 1) is in a0, and this floor's x is in s0 again.

payload.intro: The Chomper calls sqr(3). Each call to sqr will hang a new floor below the last.

rooms.prompt:
Give fact a bottom floor.
fact calls itself with x - 1. Something has to make it stop.
rooms.code_snippet: int fact(int x) { return x <= 1 ? x : x * fact(x - 1); }
rooms.hint: fact(1) is 1. Which check stops there?
rooms.explanation: Every recursive function needs a base case: an input it answers without calling itself. Without one, each call makes another, every call takes a new frame, and the tower runs off the bottom of the stack.

code.note: fact's frame: two words...
...for ra and the s0 it will borrow.

code.ask: fact is about to call itself with x - 1. Before that, stop when:

options.label: x ≤ 1 (return x)
options.why: fact(1) will skip the call and return 1, and every floor above it will multiply on the way back up.

options.label: never
options.why: With nothing to stop it, fact kept calling itself (x went 3, 2, 1, 0, -1, ...), and every call took another frame, until the tower ran off the bottom of the stack.

options.label: x ≥ 1 (return x)
options.why: x ≥ 1 was true right away, so fact(3) returned 3 without calling itself at all.

code.note: Keep x for after the call.
One floor down: fact(x - 1).
Back up: x × fact(x - 1).

payload.intro: The Chomper calls fact(3). This stack is short: 12 words.

rooms.prompt:
Follow fib(3) through both of its calls.
fib calls itself twice, and keeps values in s0 and s1 in between.
rooms.code_snippet: int fib(int n) { return n < 2 ? n : fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2); }
rooms.hint: Count the s registers fib writes.
rooms.explanation: fib keeps n in s0 and fib(n - 1) in s1 while it makes its second call, so its frame saves ra, s0, and s1. A function saves every s register it uses, however many that is.

code.ask: fib calls itself twice. It keeps n in s0, and fib(n - 1) in s1 during the second call. Its frame saves:

options.label: ra, s0, and s1
options.why: Three words per floor: the way back, and both of the caller's s registers.

options.label: ra and s0
options.why: fib wrote fib(n - 1) into s1 without saving the s1 it was given, so the Chomper got its s1 back changed. Saving s0 isn't enough when you use s1 too.

code.note: n < 2 is the base case: fib(n) = n.
Keep n.
First call: fib(n - 1).
Keep fib(n - 1) in s1 for after the second call.
Second call: fib(n - 2).
fib(n - 2) + fib(n - 1).

payload.intro: The Chomper calls fib(3). Watch the floors come and go: fib(2) goes down two more, then fib(1).

rooms.prompt:
Build fact's frame and outrun the Chomper.
The Chomper climbs up from the heap while fact(6) runs.
rooms.code_snippet: int fact(int x) { return x <= 1 ? x : x * fact(x - 1); }
rooms.hint: fact needs ra and the s0 it keeps x in. Anything more makes every floor bigger.
rooms.explanation: Two words, ra and s0, is the tightest frame that works: each of fact(6)'s floors takes 8 bytes, so the stack stays well ahead of the Chomper. Saving more still works, but every extra word is paid on every floor.

code.ask: The Chomper eats a stack word every 8 instructions, and fact(6) needs six floors. fact's frame saves:

options.label: ra and s0
options.why: Two words a floor: fact(6) has room to spare.

options.label: ra, s0, and t0
options.why: Three words a floor: fact(6) still finishes first, but by a single word.

options.label: only ra
options.why: x lived in s0, and nothing saved it: every floor multiplied by the wrong x, and the Chomper's s0 came back changed.

code.note: fact(1) is the bottom floor.

payload.intro: The Chomper calls fact(6) and starts climbing up from the heap.
